```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Triheptanoin is a medium-chain triglyceride of three seven-carbon fatty acids.
Pancreatic lipases hydrolyse it in the gut, so almost none reaches the
circulation intact; heptanoate is the most abundant and pharmacologically
active metabolite in plasma. Lee 2022 fitted a population PK model of plasma
heptanoate after oral triheptanoin in healthy adults and in pediatric and adult
patients with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD), using
Phoenix NLME (FOCE with interaction).

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Lee_2022_triheptanoin")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(mod)$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpdd.1145> (open access; PMC9795984)
* Supplement: Supplementary Tables S1-S4 and Figures S1-S2
  (`CPDD-11-1264-s001.docx`, distributed with the article).

`r rxode2::rxode2(mod)$description`

# Population

The analysis pooled 562 measurable heptanoate concentrations from 43 subject
IDs in three studies (Supplementary Tables S1 and S2): a phase 1 crossover study
in 13 healthy adults who took triheptanoin oil at 1.25 or 1.5 g/kg/day, a phase 2
study in patients with LC-FAOD, and the PK sub-study of its long-term extension.
Patients took triheptanoin with food or by gastrostomy tube at least four times
a day, at 25-35 percent of daily caloric intake. Two patients took part in two
studies and were given separate IDs.

Of the 30 LC-FAOD subjects, 23 were children or adolescents (five infants aged
6 months to under 2 years, 13 children aged 2 to under 12 years and five
adolescents) and 7 were adults (Table 2). Mean body weight was 73.8 kg in the
healthy adults, 35.0 kg in pediatric patients and 83.6 kg in adult patients
(Table 1); the overall range was 8.23-121 kg with a median of 58 kg. Twenty of
the 43 IDs (46.5 percent) were female and 35 (81.4 percent) were White.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode2(mod)$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, two parallel first-order absorption compartments, lag on the second | n/a | Figure 1; Results, Model Development |
| `lka` (Ka1) | 0.425 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lka2` (Ka2) | 0.507 1/h | Table 3 |
| `ltlag2` (Lag2) | 3.74 h | Table 3 |
| `logitfrac` (1 - F1) | F1 = 0.562 | Table 3; logit form in Table 3 footnote b |
| `lcl` (CL/F0, LC-FAOD) | 471 L/h | Table 3 |
| `e_healthy_cl` | 584 / 471 | Table 3 (CL/F0 healthy = 584 L/h) |
| `e_wt_cl` (Expo_CL) | 1.07 | Table 3 |
| `lcl_time_max` (MAX) | 0.450 | Table 3 |
| `lcl_t50` (T50) | 86.7 h | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V/F0) | 5.56 L | Table 3 |
| `e_wt_vc` (Expo_V) | 1.13 | Table 3 |
| CL/F equation | `CL/F0 * (WT/58)^Expo_CL * (1 - MAX * TIME/(T50 + TIME))` | Table 3 footnote c |
| V/F equation | `V/F0 * (WT/58)^Expo_V` | Table 3 footnote d |
| Factor 3 in `f(depot)`, `f(depot2)` | 3 mol heptanoate per mol triheptanoin | Table 3 footnote a; Methods (MW 428.61 g/mol) |
| `etalogitfrac` | 1.09 (logit-scale variance) | Table 3 and footnote b |
| `etalka` | log(1 + 1.34^2) | Table 3: BSV Ka1 = 134 percent |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.601^2) | Table 3: BSV CL/F = 60.1 percent |
| `expSd` | 0.764 | Table 3: log-additive error |

# Dosing in this model

Doses are entered in micromoles of **triheptanoin**: a dose of `D` g/kg in a
subject of `WT` kg is `D / 428.61 * 1e6 * WT` umol. The model multiplies by
three inside `f()`, so the depots receive heptanoate. Each dose needs two
records with the same amount, one to `depot` and one to `depot2`; `f()` then
splits it F1 / (1 - F1). Time `t` is the time since the first triheptanoin dose,
which the time-dependent decrease in CL/F is measured from.

```{r dose-helper}
mw_triheptanoin <- 428.61 # g/mol, Methods
dose_umol <- function(g_per_kg, wt) g_per_kg / mw_triheptanoin * 1e6 * wt

# Four doses a day with an 8-hour pause overnight (Methods, Model Application):
# the 16-hour day is split into three equal intervals of 16/3 h.
daily_dose_times <- c(0, 16 / 3, 32 / 3, 16)
n_days <- 7
dose_times <- as.vector(outer(daily_dose_times, 24 * (seq_len(n_days) - 1), `+`))
last_dose <- max(dose_times)
day7 <- 24 * (n_days - 1)

# Observation grid: every 0.25 h on day 7 and for 24 h after the last dose,
# plus the day-7 dose times so pre-dose troughs are recorded exactly.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, day7, by = 1),
  seq(day7, last_dose + 24, by = 0.25),
  day7 + daily_dose_times
)))
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper's exposure summary (Supplementary Table S4) simulates 1.25 g/kg/day
(2916 umol/kg/day) given four times a day for each analysed subject, using
their posterior Bayes parameters. The individual data are not available, so the
cohort below draws subjects from the population model instead, with body
weights matched to Table 1 (log-normal with the tabulated mean and CV;
pediatric weights truncated to the observed 8.23-121 kg range).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2022)
n_per_group <- 150

make_cohort <- function(n, group, wt_mean, wt_cv, healthy, id_offset) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + wt_cv^2))
  wt <- wt_mean * exp(rnorm(n, -sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog))
  wt <- pmin(pmax(wt, 8.23), 121)
  subj <- tibble(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), WT = wt, DIS_HEALTHY = healthy, group = group)
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = dose_times, cmt = c("depot", "depot2")) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_umol(1.25 / 4, WT))
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs)
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_per_group, "Healthy adults", 73.8, 0.176, 1L, 0L),
  make_cohort(n_per_group, "LC-FAOD adults", 83.6, 0.242, 0L, n_per_group),
  make_cohort(n_per_group, "LC-FAOD pediatric", 35.0, 0.793, 0L, 2L * n_per_group)
) |>
  # observations before doses at the same time, so a pre-dose record is a trough
  arrange(id, time, evid) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, DIS_HEALTHY, group)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "cmt")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Typical profiles over the first week

The time-dependent decrease in CL/F (up to 45 percent, T50 86.7 h) makes
heptanoate accumulate over the first days of dosing. The figure shows the
typical profile for a 58 kg subject.

```{r typical}
typical_events <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(id = 1:2, time = dose_times, cmt = c("depot", "depot2")) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_umol(1.25 / 4, 58)),
  tidyr::crossing(id = 1:2, time = seq(0, last_dose + 24, by = 0.05)) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", evid = 0L, amt = 0)
) |>
  mutate(WT = 58, DIS_HEALTHY = ifelse(id == 1, 1L, 0L)) |>
  arrange(id, time, evid)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typical_events,
                           keep = "DIS_HEALTHY") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(DIS_HEALTHY == 1, "Healthy (58 kg)", "LC-FAOD (58 kg)"))

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (day)", y = "Heptanoate (umol/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical heptanoate profile, 1.25 g/kg/day triheptanoin in four doses") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Day-7 concentration-time profile

The paper's VPC (Supplementary Figure S2) pools the observed sampling times of
each study, so it cannot be redrawn for a fixed regimen. The figure below shows
the simulated median and 90 percent interval on day 7 of the four-times-daily
regimen for each group.

```{r vpc-day7}
sim |>
  filter(time >= day7, time <= day7 + 24) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - day7, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time on day 7 (h)", y = "Heptanoate (umol/L)",
       title = "Simulated day-7 profiles: median and 5th-95th percentiles")
```

# PKNCA validation

Supplementary Table S4 reports, per group, the daily AUC (AUCday), Cmax and
Cmin at steady state, the time to Cmax and the terminal half-life after the
last dose. The day the paper treats as steady state is not stated; because
CL/F keeps falling with time, the comparison below uses day 7 (the healthy
study ran 11 days and the patient studies weeks to months). AUCday, Cmax and
Cmin are taken over day 7, Tmax over the first dosing interval of day 7, and the
half-life from the 24 hours after the last dose.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
# Time-zero records anchor PKNCA; pre-dose heptanoate is zero.
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, group, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(day7, day7, last_dose),
  end = c(day7 + 24, day7 + 16 / 3, last_dose + 24),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  cmin = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against Supplementary Table S4

Values are the medians of Supplementary Table S4.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,              ~auclast, ~cmax, ~cmin, ~tmax, ~half.life,
  "Healthy adults",    1050,     170,   62.9,  0.250, 1.74,
  "LC-FAOD adults",    1220,     288,   57.2,  0.250, 1.71,
  "LC-FAOD pediatric", 1550,     190,   78.0,  0.250, 1.69
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_long,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "umol*h/L", cmax = "umol/L", cmin = "umol/L",
            tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (day 7) vs. published (Table S4) medians. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-assert}
sim_med <- nca_long |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(value = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value) |>
  left_join(published, by = "group", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
tmax_all <- nca_long$PPORRES[nca_long$PPTESTCD == "tmax"]
stopifnot(
  # Daily exposure: a mis-transcribed CL/F, weight exponent or the factor of 3
  # moves AUCday by 50 percent or more. Across seeds and thread counts the
  # day-7 medians sat between -1 and +22 percent of Table S4.
  all(abs(sim_med$auclast_sim / sim_med$auclast_pub - 1) < 0.4),
  # Terminal half-life is absorption-limited (ln 2 / Ka1 = 1.63 h,
  # ln 2 / Ka2 = 1.37 h); observed between -18 and +1 percent of Table S4.
  all(abs(sim_med$half.life_sim / sim_med$half.life_pub - 1) < 0.3),
  # Tmax lies in Table S4's range of 0.25-4.00 h: the peak follows either the
  # dose (first sample, 0.25 h) or the opening of depot2 after its 3.74 h lag.
  all(tmax_all >= 0.25 & tmax_all <= 4.25)
)
```

AUCday and the half-life agree with Supplementary Table S4. Tmax is
bimodal: concentrations peak either at the first sample after the dose
(0.25 h) or when `depot2` opens after its 3.74 h lag, which matches Table S4's
range of 0.25-4.00 h. Which mode holds the median depends on the drawn Ka1 and
F1, so the simulated median can fall on either side; Table S4's median of
0.25 h in every group reflects the analysed subjects' individual estimates. The terminal
half-life of about 1.7 h reflects absorption, not elimination: with V/F0 of
5.56 L and CL/F0 of 471 L/h the elimination rate constant is about 85 1/h, so
plasma heptanoate follows its absorption rate (ln 2 / Ka1 = 1.63 h), and the
peak falls at the first post-dose sample (Table S4 Tmax median 0.25 h).

Cmax and Cmin are not reproduced, for two separate reasons:

- **Cmax.** The simulated medians are about 10-50 percent below Table S4. Table
  S4 summarises posterior Bayes predictions of the analysed subjects, and
  Ka1 has a 134 percent BSV with 45 percent shrinkage. The paper also notes
  that the model underpredicts the highest concentrations, most of them
  sampled within 30 minutes of a dose (Results, Figure 2). A population draw
  cannot recreate the subjects' individual absorption estimates.
- **Cmin.** Table S4 reports Cmin medians above AUCday / 24 in the same
  group (for example, healthy adults: Cmin 62.9 umol/L against an average
  concentration of 1050 / 24 = 43.8 umol/L), and its minimum Cmin in that group
  (39.7) exceeds its minimum AUCday / 24 (730 / 24 = 30.4). A subject's minimum
  cannot exceed their average, so Table S4's Cmin is not the minimum of the
  same 24-hour profile its AUCday integrates, and the definition used is not
  stated. The simulated value here is the true 24-hour minimum, reached at the
  end of the overnight pause.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose units.** Table 3 footnote a states that CL/F and V/F were corrected by a
  factor of three for the conversion of one mole of triheptanoin into three
  moles of heptanoate. The model therefore takes doses in umol of triheptanoin
  and multiplies by three in `f(depot)` and `f(depot2)`. With this reading the
  simulated AUCday matches Supplementary Table S4; without the factor it would
  be three times lower.
- **Dose split encoding.** The paper estimates F1, the fraction absorbed from
  the first compartment, on the logit scale with a variance of 1.09. The model
  carries the complementary fraction `frac = 1 - F1` routed to the delayed
  `depot2`, following the dual-absorption convention of the library. Because
  `logit(1 - F1) = -logit(F1)` and the random effect is symmetric, the two
  forms give the same distribution.
- **Residual error.** Table 3 reports the log-additive error as 0.764 without
  stating whether it is an SD or a variance; it is encoded as the SD on the
  log scale (`expSd`), the form in which Phoenix NLME reports residual error.
- **Healthy-subject CL/F.** Table 3 and Supplementary Table S3 give 584 L/h
  for healthy subjects; the Discussion quotes 544 L/h. The tables are used, and
  they also match the abstract's "about 19 percent lower" CL/F in LC-FAOD
  (471 / 584 = 0.81).
- **Time since first dose.** The time-dependent CL/F term uses time in hours
  (Table 3 footnote c). The model uses rxode2's `t`, so the simulation should
  start at the first triheptanoin dose. Patients who have taken triheptanoin
  for weeks have CL/F close to its floor of 55 percent of CL/F0.
- **Body weight.** Body weight is time-varying in the source (weight at each
  dose); the virtual cohort holds it constant over the simulated week.
- **Steady state.** The paper does not state which day its steady-state
  exposures describe; day 7 is used here (see PKNCA validation).
- **No errata.** Europe PMC lists no correction notice for this article as of
  2026-10-10.
